ARGB

This sample demonstrates using SPI and DMA to output a waveform in RETURN-TO-ZERO encoding format via MOSI, simulating the ARGB communication protocol.

In this sample, an RGB waveform for 100 pixels (assuming 100 pixels in series) is output at a refresh rate of 50 frames per second.

The system block diagram is as follows:

Requirements

The sample supports the following development kits:

Development Kits

Hardware Platforms

Board Name

RTL87x2G HDK

RTL87x2G EVB

For more requirements, please refer to Quick Start.

Wiring

Connect the SPI output pin MOSI P4_0 to the logic analyzer.

Configurations

  1. The following macros can be configured to modify pin definitions.

    #define SPI_MOSI_PIN               P4_0
#define SPI_SCK_PIN                P4_1

  2. The following macros can be configured to modify the number of ARGB LEDs and refresh rate.

    #define ARGB_LED_NUMBER          100
#define ARGB_REFRESH_RATE_HZ     50

Note

Configuration Notes: When ARGB_REFRESH_RATE_HZ is set to 50 Hz and ARGB_LED_NUMBER is 100, the time calculations are as follows:

  • Total cycle time: 20,000 us (1/50 Hz)

  • LED data transmission time: 3,000 us = 100 * 24-bit * 1.25 us

  • Reset time: 17,000 us = 20,000 us - 3,000 us

Building and Downloading

This sample can be found in the SDK folder:

Project file: samples\simulation_protocol\argb\argb_spi\proj\rtl87x2g\mdk

Project file: samples\simulation_protocol\argb\argb_spi\proj\rtl87x2g\gcc

To build and run the sample, follow the steps listed below:

  1. Open sample project file.

  2. To build the target, follow the steps listed on the Generating App Image in Quick Start.

  3. After a successful compilation, the app bin app_MP_xxx.bin will be generated in the directory mdk\bin or gcc\bin.

  4. To download app bin into EVB board, follow the steps listed on the MP Tool Download in Quick Start.

  5. Press reset button on EVB board and it will start running.

Experimental Verification

  1. After the EVB starts, observe the log information as shown in the Debug Analyzer.

    Start argb sample test!

  2. Using a logic analyzer, it can be observed that the P4_0 pin outputs 100 pixels RGB waveform every 20 ms (with a refresh rate of 50 frames per second).

Initialization

The initialization flow for peripherals can refer to Initialization Flow in General Introduction.

  1. Call Pad_Config() and Pinmux_Config() to configure the PAD and PINMUX of the corresponding pins.

    static void board_spi_init(void)
{
    Pad_Config(SPI_MOSI_PIN, PAD_PINMUX_MODE, PAD_IS_PWRON, PAD_PULL_NONE, PAD_OUT_ENABLE,
            PAD_OUT_HIGH);
    Pad_Config(SPI_SCK_PIN, PAD_PINMUX_MODE, PAD_IS_PWRON, PAD_PULL_UP, PAD_OUT_ENABLE, PAD_OUT_HIGH);

    Pinmux_Config(SPI_MOSI_PIN, SPI_MO_MASTER);
    Pinmux_Config(SPI_SCK_PIN,  SPI1_CLK_MASTER);
}

  2. Call RCC_PeriphClockCmd() to enable the ENHTIMER clock.

  3. Initialize the ENHTIMER peripheral:

    1. Define the ENHTIM_InitTypeDef type ENHTIM_InitStruct, and call ENHTIM_StructInit() to pre-fill ENHTIM_InitStruct with default values.

    2. Modify the ENHTIM_InitStruct parameters as needed. The initialization parameter configurations for ENHTIMER are shown in the table below. Call ENHTIM_Init() to initialize the ENHTIMER peripheral.

    3. Call NVIC_Init() to configure the NVIC. For NVIC-related configurations, refer to Interrupt Configuration. Call ENHTIM_ClearINTPendingBit() to clear the ENHTIM interrupt.

  1. Call RCC_PeriphClockCmd() to enable the GDMA clock.

  2. Initialize the GDMA peripheral:

    1. Define the GDMA_InitTypeDef type GDMA_InitStruct, and call GDMA_StructInit() to pre-fill GDMA_InitStruct with default values.

    2. Modify the GDMA_InitStruct parameters as needed. The initialization parameter configurations for GDMA are shown in the table below. Call GDMA_Init() to initialize the GDMA peripheral.

    3. Call NVIC_Init() to configure the NVIC. For NVIC-related configurations, refer to Interrupt Configuration.

    4. Call GDMA_INTConfig() to enable DMA Transfer interrupt.

Functional Implementation

  1. Define the argb_data to be sent. Call argb_send_frame_data to convert the 24-bit argb_data into 24 half-word argb_spi_data, and configure the DMA to prepare for transferring the converted argb_spi_data to the SPI FIFO.

    1. Set the DMA Buffer Size, DMA Source Address, and DMA Destination Address based on the input data.

    2. Each pixel consists of 24 bits (the RGB part). Each bit, depending on whether it is 1 or 0, is converted into the corresponding SPI data. The SPI is set to 12-bit transmission. According to the aRGB standard protocol, the duty cycles for 0 and 1 codes differ, thus they can be converted into corresponding SPI data, as shown in the figure.

  1. After initializing SPI and DMA, call GDMA_Cmd() to start the DMA and begin the transfer, at which point SPI starts outputting the expected waveform.

    void io_aRGB_spi_demo()
{
    board_spi_init();
    driver_spi_init();
    driver_tx_gdma_init();
    argb_send_frame_data(argb_data, sizeof(argb_data) / 4);

    GDMA_Cmd(GDMA_TX_CHANNEL_NUM, ENABLE);
}

  2. When the DMA transfer is complete, a DMA interrupt is triggered. Within the DMA interrupt, wait for the SPI data to be completely sent, then initialize ENHTIMER to start the TIMER function and set the "RESET" time.

    void ARGB_DMA_HANDLER(void)
{
//    DBG_DIRECT("into dma tx handler");
    GDMA_ClearINTPendingBit(GDMA_TX_CHANNEL_NUM, GDMA_INT_Transfer);

    while (SPI_GetFlagState(SPI_MASTER, SPI_FLAG_BUSY) == SET)
    {

    }
    driver_enhtim_init();
    argb_send_frame_data(argb_data, sizeof(argb_data) / 4);
}

  3. When the timer expires, disable the TIMER function, re-enable DMA, and SPI will continue outputting the waveform, beginning a new data refresh cycle.

    void ARGB_TIMER_HANDLER()
{
    ENHTIM_ClearINTPendingBit(ARGB_TIMER, ENHTIM_INT_TIM);
    ENHTIM_Cmd(ARGB_TIMER, DISABLE);

    GDMA_Cmd(GDMA_TX_CHANNEL_NUM, ENABLE);
}
